articles.standfirst: Planejamento, pesquisa de preços e atenção às condições de compra ajudam os visitantes a aproveitar o período de ofertas na cidade paraguaia.
articles.summary: Planejamento, pesquisa de preços e atenção às condições de compra ajudam os visitantes a aproveitar o período de ofertas na cidade paraguaia.
articles.body:
Conhecida pela variedade de lojas e produtos importados, Ciudad del Este, no Paraguai, costuma atrair consumidores brasileiros interessados em eletrônicos, informática, perfumes, acessórios e outros artigos. Durante a Black Friday, o movimento de compras ganha destaque, com oportunidades para quem deseja pesquisar produtos e encontrar opções de diferentes marcas.

Para aproveitar a visita, é importante se organizar com antecedência. Pesquisar as lojas, definir os produtos de interesse e estabelecer um orçamento são medidas que ajudam a tornar as compras mais práticas. Também vale verificar os horários de funcionamento dos estabelecimentos e considerar o tempo necessário para o deslocamento na região de fronteira.

A variedade de produtos disponíveis é um dos atrativos do comércio de Ciudad del Este. No entanto, antes de fechar uma compra, é importante comparar preços e especificações, conferir a procedência dos produtos e conhecer as condições de garantia oferecidas por cada estabelecimento.

No caso de eletrônicos e equipamentos de informática, detalhes técnicos podem fazer diferença. Processadores, memória RAM, capacidade de armazenamento e compatibilidade entre componentes são alguns dos aspectos que devem ser avaliados de acordo com a finalidade de uso.

Outro cuidado é conhecer as regras de bagagem e os limites de compras estabelecidos pela Receita Federal para quem retorna ao Brasil. Consultar as orientações oficiais antes da viagem ajuda a evitar imprevistos na fronteira.

Entre as lojas de tecnologia de Ciudad del Este, a Topdek Informática prepara uma programação especial de Black Friday para os dias 19, 20 e 21 de novembro. A agenda inclui brincadeiras, atrações, roleta interativa e sorteios de produtos, como notebooks, televisores, computadores montados, setup gamer, moto elétrica e kits de prêmios para jogos.

Localizada no Shopping Lai Lai Center, a Topdek atua no setor de informática desde 1990 e reúne produtos como notebooks, placas de vídeo, SSDs, periféricos e componentes para computadores.

Durante os três dias de campanha, os visitantes poderão conhecer as opções disponíveis na loja e participar das atividades programadas. A Topdek fica no primeiro e segundo andares do Shopping Lai Lai Center, em Ciudad del Este.

Para acompanhar as novidades da Black Friday, acesse o Instagram @topdekinformatica ou o site topdekinformatica.com.br .

articles.title: Turismo do RN tem segunda maior queda do país em setembro, aponta IBGE | G1
articles.standfirst: Atividades turísticas recuaram 3,6% em relação a agosto, segundo a Pesquisa Mensal de Serviços. Na comparação com setembro de 2025, porém, o setor potiguar registrou crescimento de 1,6%.
articles.summary: Atividades turísticas do RN recuaram 3,6% em setembro, na comparação com agosto, segundo pesquisa do IBGE. Na comparação anual, houve alta de 1,6%.
articles.body:
Turismo no Rio Grande do Norte — Foto: Sérgio Henrique Santos/Inter TV Cabugi

O volume de atividades turísticas do Rio Grande do Norte caiu 3,6% em setembro, na comparação com agosto, e registrou a segunda maior retração do país no período .

O resultado ficou atrás apenas da Bahia, que teve queda de 3,8%, segundo dados da Pesquisa Mensal de Serviços (PMS), divulgada nesta quarta-feira (11) pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

No Brasil, 13 dos estados pesquisados apresentaram resultados negativos na passagem de agosto para setembro. Apenas Alagoas (3,8%), Rio de Janeiro (2,9%) e Mato Grosso (1%) registraram crescimento. O Rio Grande do Sul ficou estável. No país, o índice de atividades turísticas recuou 1,6% no período.

Apesar da queda mensal, o turismo potiguar apresentou crescimento de 1,6% em relação a setembro de 2025. Nesse recorte, o Rio Grande do Norte teve o sétimo maior avanço do país e o terceiro do Nordeste, atrás da Bahia (17,9%) e de Alagoas (8,6%).

No acumulado de janeiro a setembro de 2026, as atividades turísticas do estado cresceram 0,9% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado. A variação acumulada em 12 meses também foi de 0,9%.

O volume de serviços do Rio Grande do Norte também apresentou queda em setembro. O índice recuou 0,8% em relação a agosto, na série com ajuste sazonal. A retração foi a quinta menor entre os 12 estados pesquisados e a primeira da região Nordeste.

Na comparação com setembro de 2025, o setor de serviços potiguar registrou queda de 4,4%. Já no acumulado de janeiro a setembro, houve crescimento de 1,3% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior.

A variação acumulada em 12 meses foi de 0,3% no estado.

A Pesquisa Mensal de Serviços acompanha o comportamento dos principais segmentos empresariais não financeiros do setor de serviços, com exceção das atividades de saúde e educação. Os dados completos podem ser consultados no Sistema IBGE de Recuperação Automática (Sidra).

articles.title: Rússia ataca rede elétrica da Ucrânia em meio a negociações | G1
articles.standfirst: Forças russas também atacaram ferrovias ucranianas, anunciou o premiê da Ucrânia. Mesmo aceitando uma tentativa de acordo trilateral, Moscou não aceitou um cessar-fogo provisório.
articles.summary: A Rússia atingiu seis instalações elétricas e ferrovias na Ucrânia durante negociações de paz mediadas pelos EUA, mas Putin recusou o cessar-fogo provisório.
articles.body:
A Rússia atacou seis grandes subestações de energia elétrica, nas quatro regiões centrais da Ucrânia , nesta quarta-feira (11), em meio ao segundo dia de negociações mediadas pelos Estados Unidos em Abu Dhabi.

A informação foi divulgada pelo primeiro-ministro ucraniano, Sergii Koretskyi, no Telegram. Segundo ele, além de atingir a infraestrutura energética do país, as forças russas também atacaram ferrovias no leste e no centro da Ucrânia.

Mesmo aceitando uma tentativa de acordo trilateral, Moscou não aceitou um cessar-fogo provisório. Nesta terça-feira (10), quando as conversas começaram, a operadora de energia ucraniana revelou que ataques contra sua infraestrutura tinham ocorrido em 8 regiões do país.

Em sua entrevista coletiva diária, o porta-voz do Kremlin afirmou, nesta quarta, que o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin , "tem sido constantemente informado pela delegação russa" sobre o andamento das negociações.

Dmitry Peskov também disse que os membros da delegação no país não estão em contato com os representantes europeus que participam do encontro em reuniões paralelas, e que não há planos para que isso aconteça.

Estados Unidos , Ucrânia e Rússia iniciaram nesta terça-feira (10) uma nova tentativa de alcançar um acordo de paz em um encontro nos Emirados Árabes Unidos que terminou com propostas conflitantes.

Negociadores russos e ucranianos se reuniram em Abu Dhabi para discurtir pontos e exigências.

👉 Segundo fontes das negociações ouvidas pela imprensa norte-americana, os EUA propuseram que a Rússia ainda fique com territórios ucranianos, mas diminua a quantidade proposta por Moscou em troca de declarar vitória no conflito.

A Ucrânia não concordou com a cessão de territórios. No entanto, o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, afirmou que as conversas foram boas.

Por parte da Rússia, também não houve nenhum sinal público de que Putin esteja disposto a abandonar sua exigência de que a Ucrânia entregue toda a região leste de Donbas antes que um acordo de paz possa ser firmado.

Os enviados especiais dos EUA Jared Kushner e Steve Witkoff com representantes dos Emirados Árabes, da Rússia e da Ucrânia. — Foto: REUTERS/Rula Rouhana

Negociadores americanos acreditam que Zelensky e Putin podem estar dispostos a chegar a um acordo sobre o território, com cada um cedendo um pouco, disse um funcionário americano à Reuters na segunda-feira.

Nos termos do acordo proposto, a Ucrânia obteria o fim da guerra, garantias de segurança e um roteiro para a adesão à UE.

O secretário de Estado americano, Marco Rubio, descreveu a reunião mediada pelos EUA como muito produtiva, sem dar detalhes.

O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, classificou as negociações como "construtivas e bastante substanciais" e disse que elas incluíram questões humanitárias e de segurança.

"A libertação de prisioneiros (de guerra) é uma prioridade. Eles falaram detalhadamente sobre a essência das garantias de segurança para a Ucrânia e as bases para garantir que essas garantias funcionem a longo prazo. São necessárias ferramentas reais para impedir qualquer recorrência da guerra. A necessidade de medidas de desescalada também foi mencionada", publicou ele no X.

articles.title: Câmara de Rio Branco aprova moção de pesar pela morte de Ayres Rocha | G1
articles.standfirst: Jornalista morreu em 14 de outubro deste ano em decorrência de um câncer. Homenagem reconhece trajetória e contribuição do profissional à comunicação e sociedade acreana.
articles.summary: Jornalista morreu em 14 de outubro deste ano em decorrência de um câncer. Homenagem reconhece trajetória e contribuição do profissional à comunicação e sociedade acreana.
articles.body:
Homenagem reconhece trajetória e contribuição do profissional à comunicação e sociedade acreana — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A Câmara de Vereadores de Rio Branco aprovou, nessa terça-feira (10), uma moção de pesar pela morte do jornalista Ayres Rocha. A homenagem tem como objetivo reconhecer a trajetória profissional e a contribuição do profissional com a comunicação e sociedade acreana.

O requerimento foi proposto por todos os vereadores e vereadoras da casa legislativa. O pedido foi aprovado por unanimidade com 14 votos dos parlamentares presentes na sessão.

Ayres Rocha morreu em 14 de outubro deste ano, aos 62 anos, em decorrência de um câncer . O jornalista foi uma dos nomes mais conhecidos do telejornalismo acreano.

Com mais de 30 anos de carreira na Rede Amazônica, ele ficou marcado principalmente pela apresentação do Jornal do Acre 2ª Edição (JAC2), onde esteve à frente da bancada por, aproximadamente, três décadas .

O Tribunal de Contas do Estado do Acre (TCE-AC) anunciou, na última quinta-feira (5), a criação do Prêmio Ayres Rocha de Jornalismo , iniciativa que pretende homenagear o jornalista acreano e reconhecer trabalhos da imprensa voltados ao controle público e à defesa dos direitos sociais.

O anúncio foi feito pela presidente do órgão, Dulce Benício, que disse que a proposta é valorizar o papel dos profissionais de comunicação na sociedade e prestar uma homenagem a Ayres Rocha.

A previsão é que o edital da premiação seja lançado em 5 de dezembro. As regras de participação, os critérios de avaliação e as categorias ainda serão detalhados no documento. A primeira edição do prêmio está prevista para 2027.

Primeira edição do prêmio de jornalismo do TCE-AC deve homenagear Ayres Rocha, que morreu aos 62 anos em Rio Branco — Foto: Divulgação

O jornalista começou a trabalhar na televisão em 1989 e se aposentou em novembro de 2024 . Em 2019, também representou o Acre em uma edição especial do Jornal Nacional , da TV Globo, durante as comemorações pelos 50 anos do telejornal. Na ocasião, dividiu a bancada com a jornalista Jéssica Senra.

Ayres morreu na madrugada de 14 de outubro de 2026, em Rio Branco, aos 62 anos . Ele fazia tratamento contra um câncer em João Pessoa, na Paraíba, e havia retornado ao Acre cerca de um mês antes da morte para ficar próximo da família.

A notícia provocou manifestações de pesar de colegas de profissão, emissoras, autoridades e instituições acreanas. O velório reuniu familiares, amigos e profissionais da imprensa na capital.

Ao longo da carreira, Ayres construiu uma relação próxima com os telespectadores e se tornou uma referência da comunicação no estado. Sua trajetória também foi marcada pelo incentivo à prevenção do câncer : após enfrentar a doença, compartilhou sua experiência publicamente e participou de campanhas de conscientização voltadas à saúde dos homens.

articles.title: Carros vindos da China já vendem duas vezes mais que os da Argentina no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: A indústria automotiva brasileira encerrou outubro com crescimento nas vendas e na produção em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025. Exportações caíram 28,3% em relação ao ano passado.
articles.summary: A indústria automotiva brasileira encerrou outubro com crescimento nas vendas e na produção em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025. Exportações caíram 28,3% em relação ao ano passado
articles.body:
De janeiro a outubro de 2026, o Brasil emplacou 288 mil veículos vindos da China, o dobro dos 143 mil trazidos da Argentina.

No mesmo período, as importações brasileiras de veículos de todas as origens chegaram a 520,7 mil unidades, alta de 29,5% em relação aos dez primeiros meses de 2025. Os dados são da Associação Nacional dos Fabricantes de Veículos Automotores ( Anfavea ).

A indústria automotiva brasileira encerrou outubro com crescimento nas vendas e na produção em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025.

Os emplacamentos subiram 1,8% e a produção avançou 2,7% . No comércio exterior, o Brasil, em relação a 2025, importou 56,7 mil veículos no mês, alta de 22,3%, e exportou 29,1 mil, queda de 28,3%.

A Argentina liderava o ranking de países de origem dos veículos importados pelo Brasil até meados de 2025. Desde então, perdeu o posto para a China.

Os modelos feitos na Argentina e importados para o Brasil são:

Renault : Kangoo e Niagara (a picape está em pré-venda)

Chevrolet : Tracker (se necessário, chega para completar a produção nacional. A GM do Brasil vai confirmar ao g1 se em 2026 houve unidades importadas)

“Estamos assistindo a uma mudança importante na dinâmica do comércio exterior, com os veículos chineses assumindo a liderança entre as origens das importações brasileiras, com o dobro do volume vindo da Argentina”, disse o presidente da Anfavea, Igor Calvet.

Calvet destacou que Brasil e Argentina mantêm uma relação de livre comércio, com vendas nos dois sentidos.

Na avaliação dele, mesmo com o Imposto de Importação de 35%, o Brasil é o país produtor que menos restringe a entrada de veículos estrangeiros . Para Calvet, isso limita o quanto as fábricas brasileiras se beneficiam do aumento das vendas no país.

Linha de produção da fábrica da Stellantis em Goiana (PE) tem produtos Fiat, Jeep e RAM — Foto: Divulgação / Stellantis

O Brasil emplacou 265,5 mil veículos e produziu 254,5 mil em outubro. Apesar da alta em relação a outubro de 2025, os dois resultados ficaram abaixo dos de setembro . As vendas caíram 5,6% e a produção recuou 5,1%.

De janeiro a outubro, os emplacamentos somaram 2,522 milhões de unidades, alta de 16,1% sobre o mesmo período de 2025. Os automóveis e comerciais leves puxaram o crescimento. As vendas do segmento passaram de 2,057 milhões para 2,412 milhões de unidades, avanço de 17,3%.

As fábricas brasileiras produziram 2,420 milhões de veículos nos dez primeiros meses do ano, cerca de 180 mil a mais que em igual período de 2025. A alta foi de 8%.

No comércio exterior, as exportações de outubro também caíram em relação a setembro, com recuo de 26,9%. As importações variaram menos na mesma comparação, com queda de 0,8%.

De janeiro a outubro, o Brasil exportou 363,1 mil veículos, 23,5% a menos que no mesmo período de 2025 . Com isso, o país importou 157,6 mil veículos a mais do que exportou. Um ano antes, as exportações superavam as importações.

Segundo a Anfavea, veículos vindos da Ásia e do México ganharam espaço nos países vizinhos , onde os fabricantes instalados no Brasil perderam participação. A queda nas vendas na Argentina, historicamente o principal destino dos veículos exportados pelo Brasil, também afetou os embarques.

As vendas de automóveis e comerciais leves eletrificados mais que dobraram no país. Foram 495,7 mil emplacamentos de janeiro a outubro, alta de 125,7% sobre o mesmo período de 2025.

A participação desses modelos nas vendas de veículos leves novos passou de 10,7% para 20,5% . Os modelos 100% elétricos, sozinhos, responderam por 7,4% do mercado de leves em 2026 até outubro.

A Anfavea também atribui parte do crescimento das vendas ao programa Carro Sustentável . Nos dez primeiros meses de 2026, o Brasil emplacou 412,8 mil unidades dos modelos contemplados, alta de 22,3% sobre o mesmo período de 2025. Esses veículos representaram 17,1% dos emplacamentos de leves no país.

Desde o início do programa, em julho de 2025, as vendas dos modelos contemplados somaram 671 mil unidades. Segundo a Anfavea, esses modelos também ficarão isentos do Imposto Seletivo.

articles.title: Richmond upon Thames is Britain's happiest place, survey finds
articles.summary: Richmond upon Thames ranked highly in several quality of life indicators in a Rightmove survey.
articles.body:
Richmond upon Thames has been named as the happiest place to live in Britain in an annual survey.

Residents of the south-west London borough have easy access to central London and strolls along the Thames on their doorstep, as well as boutiques, cafes and opportunities to spot roaming deer in their local parks.

Richmond ranked particularly highly across several aspects of local life in Rightmove's "happy at home index", including access to nature and green spaces, essential local services, shops and restaurants, employment opportunities as well as residents' pride in their area.

But, living there comes at a cost, with the average asking price for a home in the borough standing at more than £1m.

Harrogate in North Yorkshire and Cirencester in Gloucestershire came in second and third places respectively in Rightmove's 15th annual "happy at home index".

In Wales, Monmouth was the highest ranked, while Kirkcaldy took the top spot for Scotland.

Richmond returned to number one after previously winning in 2023 and finishing second last year.

Mayor of Richmond upon Thames councillor Nancy Baldwin said: "This recognition is especially meaningful because residents highlighted their pride in the local area, our beautiful parks and green spaces, and the local services they rely on every day.

"Above all, it is our people and communities that make Richmond special."

Second-placed Harrogate also ranked highly for access to nature and green spaces.

Across Britain, four-fifths (81%) of people who took part in the survey said they were happy with where they live.

People took part in the research after being emailed via Rightmove's database, so the survey was self-selecting.

Colleen Babcock, a property expert at Rightmove, said: "Richmond stands out for offering a combination many people value: easy access to nature and green spaces, without having to give up local services, places to eat and shop, or employment opportunities.

"This year's results suggest that the places people rate most highly aren't simply urban or rural, but often bring together some of the best elements of both."

articles.title: Indian-origin Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal to challenge trans sports rules: Report
articles.summary: Democratic leaders in Colorado and Washington are facing accusations of hypocrisy after signalling plans to challenge or change voter-approved
articles.body: Democratic leaders in Colorado and Washington are facing accusations of hypocrisy after signalling plans to challenge or change voter-approved restrictions on transgender athletes competing in girls' sports.According to a report by Fox News, Republicans have accused them of ignoring the people's mandate, pointing to their support for the 'No Kings' movement, which argues that political power should rest with the people and not be concentrated in the hands of leaders.The controversy erupted after voters in the two traditionally Democratic states backed measures restricting transgender students from competing in girls' school sports, the report said. However, Colorado Governor-elect Philip Weiser and Democratic Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal have both criticised the results and indicated that they would explore ways to reverse or modify the measures.Weiser suggested that Colorado's Democratic-controlled legislature could revisit the voter-approved measures. Speaking at his first post-election news conference, he said it was within the legislature's role to consider changes."It is 'statutory … and a natural and I believe appropriate role for the legislature to say ‘what are the adjustments that need to be added," he said.He also raised concerns about how the sports restriction could be implemented. "I don’t believe it would be acceptable to Colorado to have every student athlete to have to go through full-body examinations or other invasions of privacy," Weiser added, according to the Denver Post.Why are Republicans accusing Democrats of hypocrisyAs per the report by Fox News, Republicans say the Democrats' response contradicts their support for the 'No Kings' movement. The movement has organised protests against US President Donald Trump, accusing him of exercising authoritarian power and undermining democratic principles.Weiser has participated in 'No Kings' protests. Republicans argue that his willingness to revisit a decision made directly by voters goes against the movement's central message.The Adams County Republican Party called the governor-elect "King Phil I" and accused him of treating the election result as a suggestion rather than a mandate."But before the ink on the ballots is even dry, Governor-elect Phil Weiser is already signaling that the vote of the people is merely a ‘suggestion’. With Coloradans approving ballot measures to crack down on fentanyl and protect youth sports and children, Weiser walked up to the podium on Wednesday and essentially declared that the will of the majority needs to pass his personal vibe check first," the party said in a statement.The Colorado House Republican caucus also criticised the Democrats, saying: "If the Democrats truly believe there should be ‘No Kings’ in America, it is time they take their own advice."What happened in WashingtonA similar controversy has emerged in Washington state, where voters approved Initiative 638 with approximately 56% support.The measure bars students defined as "biologically male" from competing in girls' K-12 school sports. It also requires students seeking to participate in girls' teams to provide verification of their biological sex from a healthcare provider.Following the result, Jayapal said Democrats would work to reverse the measure."We're going to start planning for how we overturn these bad initiatives and how we go back to loving everyone with gender inclusivity the way we have for decades," she said, according to local media reports.Republicans and other critics pointed to Jayapal's earlier support for the 'No Kings' movement. They highlighted a November 2025 social media post in which she wrote: "We have democracy for a reason. America doesn’t belong to kings it belongs to the people and we're going to keep it that way."One critic responded: "Rep. Jayapal, this you?"Washington Democratic Party Chair Shasti Conrad has also indicated support for challenging the measure in court. She called it "unconstitutional on its face" and said the party would "support [for] organizations planning to challenge it in court."Can the voter-approved measures be reversedThe two states have different rules governing changes to ballot measures.In Colorado, the Democratic-controlled legislature could consider amendments to the voter-approved measures. Weiser has indicated that he wants lawmakers to examine possible adjustments.In Washington, lawmakers cannot repeal a voter-approved initiative during its first two years. However, they can amend it with a two-thirds majority in both legislative chambers. After two years, lawmakers can amend or repeal it with a simple majority.The controversy has put Democrats in both states in a difficult position. They must decide whether to respect the restrictions approved by voters or pursue changes through legislative and legal routes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A giant 18-metre warehouse built metres from homes in a quiet English village has left residents fighting noise and fearing lost property value; they have raised £78,000 to challenge round-the-clock truck plans
articles.summary: Residents of Astley, a village in Greater Manchester, are preparing to challenge the proposed expansion of heavy vehicle operations at warehouse complex
articles.body: Residents of Astley, a village in Greater Manchester, are preparing to challenge the proposed expansion of heavy vehicle operations at warehouse complex that has transformed their once-quiet neighbourhood. The dispute, reported by The Guardian, Wigan Today and planning publication Planning Geek, centres on an 18-metre-high distribution warehouse operated by logistics company Whistl, with residents raising £78,000 to fund legal representation at a public inquiry scheduled for November 10 and 11. The controversy has intensified since Whistl began operating from the site in July 2026. Residents say the constant movement of heavy goods vehicles, loading activity and machinery has disrupted their sleep and made parts of their homes and gardens difficult to enjoy. The warehouse, located at Astley Business Park, is among four large industrial structures built close to residential properties. Some sections of the development stand approximately 30 metres from nearby homes, leaving residents concerned about the scale of industrial activity taking place alongside their neighbourhood. The upcoming hearing will examine Whistl’s application to operate up to 60 heavy goods vehicles (HGVs) and 95 trailers from the site. According to regional reporting, 131 individuals representing 96 properties have lodged valid objections. The proceedings will be overseen by the Traffic Commissioner for the North West of England.Residents raise concerns over noise and living conditionsThe arrival of round-the-clock warehouse operations has become a major source of frustration for people living nearby. Residents have reported repeated vehicle movements, banging sounds and a persistent background hum, with some describing difficulties sleeping through the night.Former police detective Stephen Retford, who lives close to the warehouse, has documented overnight vehicle activity and commissioned an independent acoustic assessment to investigate the noise levels. Several households have also raised concerns about the impact on their mental well-being and their ability to enjoy their properties. The development has particularly affected families living close to the industrial complex. Some residents have reported that children are reluctant to use their bedrooms or gardens because of the noise and the imposing structure outside their windows.There are also growing concerns about property values. Residents fear that the proximity of the warehouse and the disruption associated with its operations could make their homes harder to sell. One household reportedly received a valuation significantly lower than its previous estimate, adding to concerns about the financial consequences of the development.How the warehouse dispute escalatedThe industrial development has been controversial since its construction began. According to Wigan Council, the land had been designated for employment-related development since 2006. An outline planning application covering residential and commercial uses was approved in 2017, while full planning permission for the warehouse development was granted in 2024.The council commissioned an independent review of the planning process after residents raised concerns about how the project had been approved. Its findings concluded that the planning decision followed the relevant legal procedures, although the council acknowledged that there were lessons to be learned regarding transparency and community engagement. The landowner, PLP, has disputed claims that the scale of the buildings changed from the plans submitted in 2023.Wigan Council has also continued discussions with residents, the landowner and Whistl. Its September update confirmed that officials had conducted site visits, investigated complaints and requested further information about measures such as acoustic fencing, landscaping and earth bunding.Whistl introduces measures to reduce disruptionWhistl has acknowledged that its initial operations affected nearby residents, particularly through nighttime noise. In response, the company agreed to pause outdoor yard operations between midnight and 6am while it works on longer-term noise reduction measures.The company has also introduced quieter electric vehicles, including an electric shunter for moving trailers, and installed noise-monitoring equipment to identify disturbances. Nighttime refuelling has been stopped, and fuel tankers are no longer permitted to access the site overnight.In a statement published on November 9, Whistl said it had taken additional steps to address residents’ concerns and was continuing to work with Wigan Council and PLP. It also confirmed that mail and parcel processing would continue inside the warehouse during the overnight pause in yard activity. The company maintains that it has operated within the conditions of its temporary operator’s licence since beginning transport operations in July.The November inquiry, however, is specifically concerned with the company’s vehicle operating arrangements and the suitability of the proposed operating centre. It is not a fresh planning appeal and will not determine whether the warehouse’s original planning permission was lawful. For residents, the proceedings represent an opportunity to have their objections formally considered and potentially secure restrictions on the scale and timing of vehicle movements. The wider dispute over noise mitigation and compliance with planning conditions remains a separate matter for Wigan Council.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: From Shah Bano to 1999 Congress revolt over foreign origin: 5 political moments in Sonia Gandhi’s memoir
articles.summary: The Shah Bano controversy, the Babri Masjid demolition and the 1999 revolt within the Congress over her foreign origin are among the political episodes
articles.body: The Shah Bano controversy, the Babri Masjid demolition and the 1999 revolt within the Congress over her foreign origin are among the political episodes Sonia Gandhi revisits in her memoir, offering her account of decisions and events that shaped the party and her own political journey.The book also recalls personal milestones, including the assassination of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi in 1991 and her subsequent withdrawal from public life. It traces how her concerns over the Congress's declining political position eventually led her to join active politics and take over as party president in 1998.In the memoir, named Belonging: A Journey of Love, five episodes stand out for their political significance, from disagreements over policy decisions during Rajiv Gandhi's tenure to the internal rebellion that threatened her leadership of the Congress in 1999.Shah Bano case (1985): Sonia questions Rajiv Gandhi's decisionSonia Gandhi recalls disagreeing with her husband, then prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, over his government's handling of the Shah Bano case.Shah Bano, a Muslim divorcee, had approached the court seeking maintenance from her husband, who had remarried and thrown her out of their home. The court ruled in her favour, but the judgement was challenged on the grounds of Muslim Personal Law.Sonia writes that she was agitated by the developments and questioned Rajiv after reading newspaper and magazine reports and hearing women activists speak in support of Shah Bano."The papers are accusing you of sacrificing Muslim women's interests. What's going on? Why are you letting this happen?" she recalls asking him.Rajiv defended his position, telling her: "Wouldn't I defend women's rights—don't you know me?"He explained that he was trying to address the concerns of women like Shah Bano without putting the entire framework of Muslim Personal Law in jeopardy. Sonia acknowledges that the compromise sought to balance religious beliefs with gender justice, but says the legal amendment overturning the court's decision was widely criticised.Babri Masjid demolition: Turning point in Sonia's political thinkingThe demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya in December 1992 and the communal violence that followed feature prominently in Sonia's account of the political developments that eventually pushed her towards public life.She describes the incident as a clear indication that the BJP-RSS and their affiliates were advancing their political agenda openly rather than working behind the scenes.Sonia connects the demolition and its aftermath with her growing concerns about the future of India's secular values and the Congress party's political position.Recalling her state of mind in the years following Rajiv Gandhi's assassination, she writes that she had repeatedly resisted calls to enter politics. However, the changing political circumstances and the weakening of the Congress began to trouble her."The India of my belonging had come to me through my husband and my mother-in-law," she writes, explaining her growing sense of responsibility towards the country and the political ideals they had upheld.1991: Rajiv Gandhi's assassinationRajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991 marked a devastating turning point in Sonia's personal life. She recalls how the Congress Working Committee met the day after his assassination and decided that she should become the party's next president. However, she had no interest in taking up the position.The Congress subsequently formed the government under P V Narasimha Rao after winning the election. Sonia remained largely secluded, with the loss of her husband leaving her unable to imagine returning to public life.Describing her state of mind, she writes: "My Rajiv was gone, nothing else mattered."She also recalls how Rahul and Priyanka tried to protect her from the media coverage surrounding the assassination and its investigation. Her grief continued for years, affecting even routine public appearances.1998: Sonia takes over as Congress presidentAfter remaining away from active politics for several years, Sonia began getting increasingly concerned about the Congress's declining position and internal divisions.She had become a primary member of the party in 1997 after attending its 80th plenary session in Calcutta at the invitation of then Congress president Sitaram Kesri.On March 14, 1998, following the Congress Working Committee's decision that a leadership change was necessary, Sonia was elected party president, replacing Kesri.She describes the transition as daunting, particularly because she had to lead a nationwide political organisation despite her limited experience in its internal functioning."I'd lived all those years in a political family, had absorbed and assimilated their core beliefs, but to be in charge of the historic Congress Party was daunting," she writes.Sonia also recalls her initial hesitation during party meetings, saying she gradually learnt to understand the organisation by listening to her colleagues and studying the issues being discussed.1999: Govt formation attempt, revolt over foreign originOne of the most significant episodes in the memoir is Sonia's account of the Congress's unsuccessful attempt to form a government in 1999 after the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led government lost a no-confidence motion by a single vote.As the leader of the largest parliamentary group, Sonia was tasked with exploring the possibility of forming an alternative government. She writes that the Congress and its allies had a combined strength of 233 MPs, while other parties had assured support to take the tally to the required majority of 272 in the 543-member Lok Sabha.However, the promised support failed to materialise. Reflecting on the episode, she admitted: "Nevertheless, it was a miscalculation on my part. Our group was depending on assurances given by certain persons, and those were not fulfilled."The political setback was followed by another crisis within the Congress. In May 1999, Sonia received a letter jointly sent by three Congress Working Committee colleagues, the most prominent among them Sharad Pawar, questioning her eligibility to hold high office because she was foreign-born.The issue was raised again at a CWC meeting, leaving Sonia deeply hurt. She recalls that she walked out of the meeting with tears in her eyes and subsequently submitted her resignation.In her resignation letter, she wrote that although she had been born in a foreign land, she had chosen India as her home and would remain Indian to her last breath.Sonia says it was not the question of holding high office that hurt her, but the questioning of her loyalty to India. Following appeals from party workers and colleagues, she eventually agreed to continue as Congress president. The three leaders were suspended, while Pawar later broke away to form the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP).Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2026, brothers Tjerayh and Tjeryan Coleman-Ware opened Ceduna's first new barber shop in 50 years; the Aboriginal-owned business grew from haircuts they practised in their family shed
articles.summary: Hair has always been important to how we feel about ourselves, and two brothers in Australia know just how to make someone feel confident about their look
articles.body: Hair has always been important to how we feel about ourselves, and two brothers in Australia know just how to make someone feel confident about their look through a haircut. For brothers Tjerayh and Tjeryan Coleman-Ware, the need for a good haircut first brought them towards barbering. Now, in 2026, the two have turned that early interest into a business of their own, opening Ceduna's first barber shop in nearly 50 years. Their shop, ThaBruthaz Barbershop, is also the only 100 per cent Aboriginal-owned and operated shop on the town's main street.According to a report by NewsDive in Australia, dated November 6, 2026, the brothers have brought a service back to the South Australian town after a gap of five decades, with their journey beginning much closer to home than the shop they now operate.A passion that started at homeTjerayh was just 15 when he first picked up a pair of clippers. Growing up with his brothers, there was no one available to cut their hair, so they would take turns giving each other haircuts.It was not only about learning to cut hair or getting the right style, as Tjerayh also enjoyed seeing what difference a haircut could make to someone's confidence. As his interest grew, he began cutting hair in the shed at his family home, learning the trade on his own at first. Then, as more boys from the neighbourhood and their extended family started coming in for haircuts, he was able to hone his skills and learn more advanced cuts. All this while, his younger brother Tjeryan was watching this develop from the sidelines, and eventually, he too became interested in learning the trade. What had started as Tjerayh's individual interest was gradually becoming something the two brothers could work towards together.From the family shed to a businessIn 2024, Tjerayh came across an opportunity through the Ceduna Aboriginal Corporation (CAC), which was offering local people the chance to complete a Certificate III in Beauty and Barbering. The organisation, a community-controlled, not-for-profit corporation, has been working towards social and economic reform for Aboriginal people in the Ceduna region.Both brothers decided to take up the opportunity in 2025 and pursued the course. They received their qualifications in 2026, eventually leading them to open their own shop. Tjerayh recalled how quickly they wanted to complete the training, saying they had pretty much flown through everything as fast as they could.More than just a place for haircutsThe opening also carries a significance beyond the brothers' personal journey. Tha Bruthaz Barbershop is the only 100 per cent Aboriginal-owned and operated shop on Ceduna's main street, giving the family a place of their own in the town's commercial centre.For many of the brothers' early customers, however, the new shop is not the first time they have seen the two at work. Ceduna resident Daniel Newchurch-Lawrie has known them for years and has been getting haircuts from them since their early days. He remembered how Tjerayh initially gave the boys simple haircuts before gradually becoming more skilled and experimenting with more technical styles. Football season was often a reason for the boys to approach him for a fresh cut.The family ties are also noticeable in the way they support the business. A younger cousin comes into the shop after school to help sweep the floors, while a small stand on the counter displays earrings made by the brothers' mother and younger sister. It is a detail that makes the shop feel connected to the family that helped bring it into existence, rather than simply being a place where customers come and go.There are also plans for the shop to become a place for people to come together. According to ABC's November 6 radio report, local Aboriginal service Yadu Health is set to hire the premises for a special event called 'Clip and Yarns' during November. The idea is to bring people into the shop, where they can get their hair cut, have a conversation and spend time together.For Tjerayh and Tjeryan, the journey from taking turns cutting each other's hair at home to opening their own shop has taken years of practice, training and patience. Today, their new business has become a place where they can not only realise the dream they once harboured but also continue working on their craft in a community that has come to support them.You use AI every day. articles.title: Kazakh-linked hackers use AI to steal over 2,000 sensitive files from Tajik govt
articles.summary: A hacking group suspected of operating from Kazakhstan used an artificial intelligence (AI) agent to break into a government document system in
articles.body: A hacking group suspected of operating from Kazakhstan used an artificial intelligence (AI) agent to break into a government document system in neighbouring Tajikistan and steal more than 2,000 sensitive files, cybersecurity firm CloudSek said in a report published on Wednesday.The Singapore-based company said it uncovered the operation after the hackers accidentally left one of their servers accessible on the internet. Investigators found that the group had used Hermes, an open-source framework that allows AI agents to carry out tasks independently, to plan and execute the cyberattack.The discovery suggests that the use of AI in cybercrime is no longer limited to ordinary criminals, with groups involved in more sophisticated espionage operations also turning to the technology.“Instead of typing hacking commands by hand, the attacker told Hermes what to do, and Hermes planned the attacks, wrote the rules, ran them, kept notes, and wrote up reports,” CloudSek told news agency Reuters.The governments of Kazakhstan and Tajikistan did not immediately respond to requests for comment.According to CloudSek, the hackers began using Hermes to gather information about their targets around the middle of August. Within a few weeks, they had gained access to Tajikistan's electronic document system.The AI agent then developed a customised programme to download the documents, sort them and divide them into smaller sections. This helped the hackers collect and steal the files more efficiently, the company said.The exposed server also contained instructions that the hackers had given the AI agent, including details about its role, how it should work and how it should communicate with them.“You are an elite offensive security specialist and red teamer,” one of the instructions read. A red teamer is a cybersecurity expert who carries out simulated attacks to identify weaknesses in an organisation's security systems.CloudSek identified the group as 'Silent Lynx', a name used by researchers to track the hackers. Other cybersecurity researchers have previously linked the group to Kazakhstan.The company said it based its assessment on several clues. These included the hackers' use of the Russian language, their activity during typical Kazakh business hours and their frequent access to the exposed server through an internet connection registered to a residential user in Kazakhstan.You use AI every day. articles.title: Heatwaves predicted to cost London £25bn in next decade
articles.summary: Mayor Lord Khan will ask global leaders at COP31 to do more to tackle extreme temperatures.
articles.body:
Continued heatwaves in London could cost the capital more than £25bn over the next decade, the city's mayor Lord Khan has warned.

City Hall has estimated the cost of lost productivity, as analysis revealed London's 2026 heatwaves alone cost about £2.5bn.

London's mayor is expected to call on global leaders at COP31 in Antalya to step up action to tackle the climate emergency and protect cities from extreme temperatures.

Speaking at the World Leaders' Summit, Lord Khan will urge politicians to match the scale of the challenge with investment.

"The climate sceptics argue that these investments are unaffordable," he will say in his COP address.

"But the only thing we cannot afford is to do nothing. Because, even if you can see past the devastating implications for human health, the long-term economic impact of extreme heat alone will be astronomical.

"If the scenes we saw this summer became the standard, it could cost London's economy more than £25bn over the next 10 years."

In London, the mayor is working with boroughs and other partners to prepare the capital for hotter summers and protect those most at risk.

Heat Ready London, produced with London Councils and published this summer, sets out priorities including reducing overheating in homes.

Tom Edwards, BBC London environment correspondent

What the mayor is telling world leaders is that not tackling climate change and reducing carbon emissions will cost economies and cities much more in the long run.

After another sweltering summer in the capital, he wants more investment in climate resilience and cutting emissions.

There is talk in London about reducing overheating in homes and essential public buildings, protecting frontline workers and creating more shade.

While there has been some progress, the financial bill for many of the remediations like retrofitting homes is huge and observers say it's not yet clear who will pay.

articles.title: Reviving the American Dream? What Democrat-held Congress really means for migrants & Indians
articles.summary: Democrats have taken control of both chambers of the US Congress, setting up a major confrontation with President Donald Trump over his hardline
articles.body: Democrats have taken control of both chambers of the US Congress, setting up a major confrontation with President Donald Trump over his hardline immigration agenda.From mass deportations and detention policies to asylum restrictions and legal pathways for migrants, the incoming Democratic majority could reshape the debate over immigration. However, a change in congressional control does not automatically mean an end to Trump's policies.Trump will remain in the White House for another two years, retain control over federal immigration agencies and have billions of dollars already approved for enforcement operations. For immigrants, including Indian professionals navigating work visas and green card backlogs, the question is whether the political shift will bring meaningful relief or simply open another chapter in America's bitter immigration debate.What Democrats want to change in Trump's immigration policyDemocrats are preparing to use their congressional majority to challenge Trump's immigration agenda, focusing on investigating enforcement operations and developing an alternative vision for immigration reform.According to the Associated Press, incoming lawmakers are considering investigations into Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), detention conditions, alleged enforcement abuses and the agency's recruitment of thousands of deportation officers. Control of congressional committees will also give Democrats greater authority to summon witnesses, demand documents and scrutinise the administration through oversight hearings.The push is expected to extend beyond investigations. Some Democrats want to revive efforts to create a pathway to citizenship for long-term undocumented immigrants and expand opportunities for legal immigration.Senator-elect James Talarico of Texas told Fox News after the election that the country needed comprehensive immigration reform, including a pathway to citizenship for people who had lived and worked in the US without legal status for years.Representative Gabe Vasquez of New Mexico has proposed creating new visa categories for workers providing childcare and elderly care. Speaking to AP, Vasquez argued that immigration reform could address labour shortages while giving eligible migrants a legal route to work and remain in the country.Representative Robert Garcia, who is set to lead the House Oversight Committee, has also identified investigations into alleged abuses by immigration authorities as a priority. These could examine spending on detention facilities, ICE recruitment and training procedures, and deaths in immigration custody.However, Democrats have yet to agree on a unified legislative programme. Sarah Pierce, director of social policy at Washington-based think tank Third Way, told AP that the party needed to combine oversight with "a proactive vision for what immigration should look like in the United States."From mass deportations to targeted enforcementOne of the most significant changes Democrats could pursue is a shift away from Trump's sweeping deportation drive towards a more targeted approach to immigration enforcement.Under such a system, authorities would give priority to removing individuals considered threats to national security or public safety, rather than pursuing undocumented immigrants indiscriminately. It could also lead to a reassessment of how people who have lived and worked in the US for years are treated.The approach draws partly on enforcement priorities introduced under former president Joe Biden. In September 2021, the Department of Homeland Security issued guidelines directing immigration authorities to prioritise national security threats, public safety threats and recent border crossers.The guidelines gave immigration officers greater discretion in deciding whom to pursue for deportation. A federal district court struck them down in June 2022, but the Supreme Court reversed that decision in June 2023, ruling that Texas and Louisiana lacked the legal standing to challenge the policy. Importantly, the Supreme Court did not rule on the merits of the enforcement priorities themselves.For the incoming Democratic majority, an immediate priority is likely to be greater scrutiny of how ICE identifies, arrests and detains immigrants. Congressional investigations could establish whether enforcement operations are sweeping up people without serious criminal records and whether existing legal safeguards are being followed.Citizenship, DACA and asylumOne of the biggest questions facing the incoming Democratic majority is whether it can revive efforts to provide legal status to undocumented immigrants who have lived in the United States for years.In 2021, former president Joe Biden introduced the US Citizenship Act, which proposed an eight-year pathway to citizenship for eligible undocumented immigrants. The legislation also included provisions for Dreamers, farmworkers and people holding Temporary Protected Status. However, it failed to advance through Congress.The Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) programme could become another priority. Introduced under Barack Obama in 2012, DACA protects eligible immigrants brought to the US as children from deportation and allows them to obtain work authorisation.Biden attempted to strengthen the programme through a federal rule in 2022, but it faced legal challenges. According to US Citizenship and Immigration Services, existing recipients can continue applying for renewals, while new applications cannot currently be approved under court orders.House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has also indicated that restoring protections for DACA recipients and people covered by Temporary Protected Status could provide a starting point for negotiations with the Trump administration, according to TIME.Asylum policy is another potential flashpoint. Democrats could seek to restore broader access to asylum processing, although Biden's own record illustrates how politically complicated the issue remains.In June 2024, his administration introduced restrictions limiting asylum eligibility for certain migrants crossing the southern border unlawfully when migrant encounters exceeded specified thresholds. The measures, documented by the Congressional Research Service, demonstrated that Biden had also moved towards tighter border controls towards the end of his presidency.For Democrats, the challenge will be to balance legal pathways and humanitarian protections with stronger border management. Whether any of these proposals become law will ultimately depend on negotiations with Republicans and Trump's willingness to sign the legislation.What could a Democratic Congress mean for Indian migrants, students & H-1B professionals?The outcome of the US midterms could have implications for India well beyond Washington's political battle over deportations. Indian nationals make up a significant share of America's skilled foreign workforce, particularly in the technology sector, while hundreds of thousands of Indian students depend on US universities and post-study employment opportunities.According to the Migration Policy Institute (MPI), around 3.2 million Indian immigrants lived in the US in 2024, making them the country's second-largest foreign-born population. Indian nationals accounted for 71 per cent of approved H-1B petitions in fiscal year 2024, according to data cited by the Council on Foreign Relations. More than 363,000 Indian students were enrolled in US higher education institutions during the 2024-25 academic year, MPI reported.One of the biggest concerns for Indian professionals is the H-1B visa programme, which allows US employers to recruit foreign workers for specialised occupations. Democrats could push for a review of stricter visa selection and wage requirements introduced under Trump, although such a move has not emerged as a unified party commitment.Indian students are another group vulnerable to changes in immigration policy. Tighter scrutiny of student visa applications, longer interview waits and uncertainty over post-study employment opportunities can complicate plans for those hoping to study and subsequently work in the US.However, one of the most persistent challenges for Indian professionals is the employment-based green card backlog. The US immigration system's per-country limits have contributed to particularly long waiting periods for Indian applicants, leaving many professionals dependent on temporary visas for years while awaiting permanent residency.Democrats could reopen discussions on increasing employment-based visa availability or changing country-wise limits. But such changes would require legislation and cannot be delivered by the president alone.For Indian migrants, therefore, a Democratic-controlled Congress could create an opportunity to revisit longstanding immigration concerns. It does not, however, guarantee an immediate improvement in visa access, work opportunities or permanent residency prospects.Can Democrats turn congressional control into immigration reform?The Democratic victory has opened a new front in the battle over America's immigration policy. But while the party will have greater powers to challenge the administration, it will not control the agencies responsible for implementing Trump's deportation agenda.When the new Congress convenes on January 3, 2027, Democrats will be able to use committee investigations, subpoenas and oversight of future spending decisions to scrutinise immigration enforcement. The administration, however, will retain control over ICE, Customs and Border Protection, and the Department of Homeland Security.The financial backing for Trump's crackdown presents another major obstacle. According to AP, Republicans approved around $150 billion in 2025 to expand immigration detention capacity, complete the border wall and recruit thousands of deportation officers. Further multi-year funding for ICE and Border Patrol was also enacted in 2026.Trump has recently signalled that he could be open to an immigration deal. In an interview with CBS's 60 Minutes, he acknowledged that his administration's mass deportation policy might have been "too tough" and suggested discussing an arrangement for some immigrants who have lived in the country for 10 or 15 years. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has also indicated a willingness to engage in discussions with Democrats.However, these signals have been met with scepticism. Trump's elevation of Stephen Miller, the architect of his hardline immigration agenda, to White House chief of staff has raised questions about how far the administration is prepared to go in making concessions.Even if Democrats manage to pass immigration legislation through both chambers, Trump retains the power to veto it. Congress can override a presidential veto only with a two-thirds majority in both the House and Senate, a threshold Democrats are unlikely to reach. Most major legislation in the Senate also faces a 60-vote hurdle to overcome a filibuster.The political shift could therefore mean greater scrutiny of deportations, investigations into enforcement practices and renewed debate over legal pathways. But it is unlikely to translate into an immediate change in the immigration status of millions of people.For Indian students and professionals, much will depend on whether Democrats can turn discussions around skilled-worker visas, student mobility and green card backlogs into concrete legislative proposals.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘I am safe, receiving treatment’: President’s bodyguard Saurabh Tomar after being shot in UP
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Army jawan Saurabh Tomar, serving in the President’s Bodyguard (PBG) regiment, has said he is safe and undergoing treatment in Meerut after
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Army jawan Saurabh Tomar, serving in the President’s Bodyguard (PBG) regiment, has said he is safe and undergoing treatment in Meerut after being shot in the head allegedly by two neighbours in Uttar Pradesh’s Baghpat on Diwali night.Speaking to ANI, Saurabh said, “I am serving in the President’s Bodyguard. A man named Dheeraj, who belongs to my village, shot me. I have lodged a complaint at the local police station, and the police have responded. I am currently receiving medical treatment in Meerut, and I am safe.”The 28-year-old soldier, who is part of the mounted unit stationed at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi, was visiting his native village, Gopalpur Khadana, when the incident took place. He and his brother Vineet were standing outside their house when two neighbours, identified as Dheeraj and Monu alias Praveen, allegedly confronted them over an old rivalry.According to his brother Vineet, the family was sitting outside their home when the accused arrived and got into an argument with them. One of the men allegedly pulled out a country-made weapon and shot Saurabh when he came outside. Vineet also suffered serious head injuries after being attacked with a stick.Saurabh underwent surgery at a hospital in Meerut on Monday and was declared out of danger. Police have registered an attempt-to-murder case against the two accused, who remain at large.Baraut Circle CO Anshu Jain said police received information around 10pm on November 8 that two individuals, Sonu and Dheeraj, had shot and injured a local resident in Gopalpur Khadana village.President’s Bodyguard is the Indian Army’s senior-most regiment in the order of precedence. Based at Rashtrapati Bhavan, the cavalry unit performs ceremonial escort and security duties for President of India. articles.title: Four bears killed in Canada after attack on mother and daughter
articles.summary: The sow and her three cubs were responsible for killing Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20, earlier this month.
articles.body:
Four grizzly bears have been killed in connection with a fatal attack on a mother and daughter in the Canadian province of British Columbia.

Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20, died earlier this month after going on an afternoon walk in a trail area in Bella Coola.

The British Columbia Conservation Office Service (BCCOS) launched an investigation into their deaths and forensic testing has since confirmed a sow and her three cubs were responsible for the attack.

All four were destroyed "in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines" to protect the public, BCCOS Inspector Jeff Tyre said in an update on Tuesday.

Mother and daughter die after suspected grizzly bear attack in Canada

"Evidence from the investigation as well as animal DNA was analysed and conclusively linked to a sow and its three offspring," he added.

The attack "likely involved predatory behaviour", which Tyre said was "very rare".

He added that more than a dozen conservation officers took part in the investigation over the past week, amid "difficult terrain and weather".

Balcarras and Reed were "two peas in a pod" who "got along really, really well" and shared many hobbies, Balcarras' brother, Josh, told CBC.

"When Jenny hiked, Selah was right there beside her," he said.

Tyre said DNA testing also confirmed the four bears were not involved in a 2025 attack on a school group also in the Bella Coola area.

The incident in November of last year saw 11 people injured, two of them critically, while the bear responsible was never found.

"Today, we have learned from the BC Conservation Officer Service members that they have captured and euthanized the bears involved in the recent fatal attack," said Samuel Schooner, Elected Chief of the Nuxalk Nation, in a statement.

"We would like to thank the BC Conservation Officer Service for their dedication and hard work to resolve this incident. This attack has been deeply re-triggering for our community members as we continue to recover from last year's attack. Our thoughts remain with the victims' families."

articles.title: EasyJet shareholders approve £5.7bn takeover
articles.summary: The Luton-based carrier will fall under US ownership once the deal is completed.
articles.body:
EasyJet shareholders have approved the airline's £5.7bn takeover by private equity firm Apollo, paving the way for it to fall into US ownership.

The Luton-based carrier said 97.07% of shareholders voted in favour of the takeover by the US investment group at a meeting of its investors on Wednesday.

According to the airline the deal will be completed by the end of March next year.

In August EasyJet's board agreed to Apollo's offer of 715p a share , the US investment group also owns The Restaurant Group, which operates Wagamama.

The deal will end the company's more than 26 years on the London stock market and see EasyJet fall into US ownership.

The low-cost airline is understood to be consulting on proposals that could see up to about 50 head office roles axed out of a 2,300-strong team.

Apollo secured the deal after winning in a takeover tussle with US investment firm Castlelake.

Castlelake had previously made a £5.5bn, or 690p a share, proposal to buy EasyJet, but walked away from the bidding war in August.

EasyJet was founded by Sir Stelios Haji-Ioannou in 1995 as a low-cost air travel alternative and it has since expanded to be one of the largest networks across Europe.

Sir Stelios and his family, who own just over 15% of the business, have backed the takeover.

articles.summary: The number of Wood Whites spotted in area where it has been reintroduced rockets from 73 to 746.
articles.body:
A wildlife charity says numbers of a rare butterfly in a wood have "boomed", exploding by 922% after it was reintroduced.

Butterfly Conservation (BC) said it had recorded 746 Wood Whites at Fineshade Wood in Rockingham Forest, near Corby, Northamptonshire, compared to just 73 in 2025.

Twenty adult Wood Whites, a butterfly classified as endangered in Great Britain , had been taken to the Forestry England site in 2024 from Hazelborough Forest and Bucknell Wood, close to Silverstone.

The charity said the tally of recent sightings had been "absolutely extraordinary" and heat "may have turbo-charged larval growth".

BC said male Wood Whites performed "courtship displays in which they land opposite females, extend their tongue-like proboscis and wave their head and antennae back and forth over the female's wings".

The butterfly used to be much more common across southern England and eastern Wales, but since 1992 its distribution has dropped by 76%.

Dr Jamie Wildman, BC's central England conservation manager, said: "The number of butterflies being seen by our volunteers and members of the public is absolutely extraordinary.

"We're delighted to see the population boom so quickly since the start of the reintroduction.

"Only two years ago we were releasing butterflies here in the hope that one day the woodland would support a thriving population again.

"Seeing hundreds of Wood Whites flying through Fineshade today shows what's possible when habitat restoration, scientific research and hundreds of volunteer hours come together."

The reintroduction was made possible by funding from Natural England's Species Recovery Programme.

The charity said on 15 July one volunteer had counted no fewer than 42 Wood Whites, thought to be offspring of the first brood, which hatched in May.

BC believes the warm spring might have accelerated caterpillar development.

Dr Dan Hoare, its director of nature recovery, said: "If the ground is wet enough to start with and the foodplants are in the ditch edge, sheltered and supported by taller grasses, then the heat may have turbo-charged larval growth and helped them get through before the worst of it.

"As butterflies are so sensitive to temperature, tracking their fortunes can provide crucial insights on which species might be winners and losers from our rapidly changing climate, helping us plan effective climate adaptation."

If the success continued, the charity said Fineshade Wood would be a "beating heart" for the Wood White, sending butterflies out into the surrounding countryside and woodland.

Mark Underwood, forest centre manager at Fineshade Wood, said: "I know anecdotally Forestry England staff and our visitors have been spotting lots of these beautiful butterflies.

"We're proud to partner with Butterfly Conservation on such a successful reintroduction."

articles.title: NFL star Jessie Bates III pledges $1 million over four years to support single mothers in Atlanta and his hometown, inspired by his own mother who raised six children while working two jobs
articles.summary: When NFL players make a move to a new city, their commitments often extend beyond the football field.
articles.body: When NFL players make a move to a new city, their commitments often extend beyond the football field. For Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III, joining a new team in 2023 also marked an opportunity to continue a cause that had been important to him long before his professional career began. Having grown up in a household led by a single mother, Bates wanted to support women facing the responsibility of raising children on their own. He announced plans to give $1 million over four years to organisations working with single mothers in Atlanta and his hometown of Fort Wayne, Indiana, building on a charitable initiative he had already established in Cincinnati.Jessie Bates' $1 million commitment to single mothersAs reported by Atlanta Falcons Football Club, Bates made the pledge on 16 March 2023, the day he arrived at the Atlanta Falcons' training facility in Flowery Branch to complete his move to the team. His four-year contract was worth $62.04 million, and he planned to dedicate part of his earnings to community organisations supporting single-parent families.The money was to be distributed over the length of the contract, with organisations in the Atlanta area and Fort Wayne set to benefit. Rather than establishing an entirely new charitable programme, Bates intended to continue the work of his existing JB3 Single Mother's Initiative, which focuses on recognising and assisting women bringing up children without a partner.For safety, the commitment was connected to an experience he had known throughout childhood. His mother, Theresa, raised Bates and his five siblings while working two jobs to provide for the family. Her efforts remained a significant influence on how he approached his own success and what he wanted to do with it.How his mother's experience shaped the JB3 initiativeBates grew up in Fort Wayne, Indiana, in a family where his mother carried much of the responsibility for raising six children. The demands of managing work and family life gave him an understanding of the practical difficulties single parents can face.That background eventually led him to establish the JB3 Single Mother's Initiative. Its purpose was to acknowledge the work of single mothers and provide families with experiences and support they might otherwise struggle to afford.The initiative became particularly visible during the 2022 NFL season, when Bates arranged a weekend of activities for six single mothers and their children in Cincinnati. The event was organised around giving the families time together while providing assistance in several different ways.The mothers and children were taken shopping, while the youngsters received haircuts. Bates also arranged a private cinema screening and other activities for the group. The weekend was intended to give the families a break from their usual routines and recognise the responsibilities the mothers handled.NFLPA recognised his community work in 2022The Cincinnati event helped Bates receive the NFL Players Association's Community MVP recognition during Week 15 of the 2022 season.The award acknowledged his efforts to organise the weekend through the JB3 initiative. It also brought attention to a side of his professional life that he wanted to develop alongside his football career.At the time, Bates was completing his fifth season in the NFL. He had joined the league after being selected by the Cincinnati Bengals in the second round of the 2018 NFL Draft and had spent the first part of his career with the team.His community work had already been shaped by his personal experiences, but the recognition gave the initiative a wider platform. His plans for Atlanta meant that the programme would reach beyond Cincinnati, extending its work to another city where he would be living and playing.Why Bates wanted to continue the work in AtlantaMoving to the Falcons offered Bates a chance to build relationships in a different community while maintaining his involvement in charitable work. He spoke about wanting to contribute outside the locker room, rather than measuring his influence solely through performances on the field.His announcement also reflected the connection between his upbringing and the families he hoped to assist. The support he received from his mother had shaped his understanding of what a parent might sacrifice to give children a stable home.Speaking about the commitment, Bates described the initiative as something he cared deeply about. He also said that his earlier work in Cincinnati had allowed him to do things for other families that he had long wanted to do with his own mother by his side.You use AI every day. articles.title: Centre simplifies visa regime: Paperwork cut by 70%, categories reduced from 13 to 9
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Centre has simplified India's visa regime, reducing the number of main visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23, in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Centre has simplified India's visa regime, reducing the number of main visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23, in a move aimed at making travel, education and medical treatment in the country easier for foreign nationals.The ministry of home affairs (MHA), in a press release on Wednesday, said the number of fields to be filled in visa application forms across all 23 sub-categories has been reduced by 65-70%, making the process easier, faster and more applicant-friendly.This follows an earlier rationalisation in October 2025, when the number of main visa categories was reduced from 22 to 13 and sub-categories from 63 to 49.Student visa category reorganisedAs part of the changes, the Student Visa category has been consolidated into two broad sub-categories — S-1 and S-2.The S-1 Visa covers school, graduate and post-graduate education, while the S-2 Visa covers PhD scholars and research students in Indian universities, visiting faculty, foreign research students visiting India, scientific and anthropological expeditions, internships and exchange programmes, among other specified academic activities.Foreign students enrolled in Indian educational institutions through the Study in India portal may be granted an e-S1 Visa for up to five years or for the duration of their academic course, whichever is shorter. The visa will allow multiple entries.Under the revised framework, the erstwhile Tourist Visa has been renamed the Visitor Visa. Provisions relating to medical, student and business visas have also been reorganised.The MHA is updating its information technology systems to implement the revised framework, with visas under the new system expected to be issued by the end of 2026.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
