articles.title: A Louisiana father left his estate to his wife in a 2015 will, but six of his nine children challenged the document's signatures; an appeals court has reversed a ruling voiding the will and ordered further hearings
articles.summary: A disagreement over a father's signature on his will turned into a lengthy inheritance dispute in Louisiana, after six of his nine children challenged a
articles.body: A disagreement over a father's signature on his will turned into a lengthy inheritance dispute in Louisiana, after six of his nine children challenged a document that left his estate to his surviving wife. The children questioned whether the will had been properly signed and witnessed, arguing that the difference between the printed name on its first page and the cursive signature on its second page made it legally invalid.In a November 6, 2026, ruling available on Justia, the Louisiana Court of Appeal, First Circuit, reversed a lower court judgment that had declared the October 20, 2015, will invalid and an absolute nullity. The appeals court found that the children had not provided sufficient evidence to establish that the document failed to meet the applicable legal requirements. It sent the case back to the trial court for further proceedings.How the inheritance dispute beganLouis Edward Lloyd Sr. died on July 19, 2021, leaving behind his wife, Evelyn Robertson Lloyd, and nine children. Three of the children were born during his marriage to Evelyn, while the remaining six were from another relationship. On December 1, 2021, Evelyn filed a petition asking the court to recognise her as the sole legatee under her husband's October 2015 will. The document left all his separate and community property to her. On December 7, 2021, the trial court granted her petition and placed her in possession of the estate.However, six of Lloyd's children challenged the arrangement in October 2022. They filed a petition seeking to annul the probated will and reopen the succession proceedings. Among their arguments was that their brother, Louis E Lloyd Jr., was totally disabled and qualified as a forced heir under Louisiana law.In July 2024, the trial court separately recognised Louis E Lloyd Jr. as a forced heir. The children also maintained that their father's will was invalid because of problems with its signatures and execution.Why the children challenged the signaturesThe main dispute concerned the way Lloyd's name appeared on the two-page document. The children argued that his name was printed on the first page, while a cursive signature appeared on the second page. They claimed that the difference meant the will did not satisfy the legal requirements for a valid notarial testament.They also questioned whether the document had been signed in the presence of a notary and two witnesses. Their concerns extended to another version of the will, which carried a 'True Copy' stamp and contained differences in the names of some family members.The notary who prepared the document, Linda E Hodge, testified that Lloyd had read the will and signed it in front of two witnesses, Marsha Strickland and Eugene Hodge Sr. She identified the separate 'True Copy' version and explained that it contained typographical errors, including an incorrect name for one of Lloyd's children. However, Hodge could not clearly remember why the document had been stamped 'True Copy' or whether the witnesses remained present while she corrected the errors and prepared the final version.Why the appeals court reversed the decisionOn January 31, 2025, the six children sought partial summary judgment, asking the court to declare the will absolutely null. The trial court granted their request on April 3, 2025, and later issued an amended judgment on August 12, 2026, formally declaring the will invalid. Evelyn appealed, arguing that the children had failed to prove the document was legally defective. She also maintained that the burden of establishing the will's invalidity rested with those challenging it, not with her.The appeals court examined Louisiana's Civil Code and an important legislative change that took effect on August 1, 2025. The revised Article 1576 simplified the requirements for notarial wills. Under the amended provision, a will must be written, dated and executed before a notary in the presence of two witnesses, with signatures from the testator, both witnesses and the notary.The revised law removed the requirement that the person making the will sign every separate page. It also eliminated the attestation clause as a condition of validity. Importantly, the legislation applied retroactively to pending claims, provided they had not already been decided through a final judgment. Since the children's challenge was still pending when the amendments took effect, the appeals court held that the revised requirements applied.After examining the will, the judges found that it appeared to have been written, dated and signed by Lloyd, the two witnesses and the notary. The evidence presented by the children did not establish that Lloyd had failed to sign the document or that it had not been properly executed. The court also noted that the existence of the separate 'True Copy' version did not prove that the actual will was invalid. Under Louisiana law, those challenging a notarial testament carry the burden of proving its invalidity, and the children had failed to meet that requirement.What happens nextThe Louisiana Court of Appeal reversed the August 12, 2026, amended judgment that had annulled Lloyd's 2015 will. It remanded the case for further proceedings and assessed the costs of the appeal against the six children. The ruling does not finally settle every issue concerning the estate or remove the separate forced-heirship determination. Instead, it overturns the judgment that had declared the will invalid, allowing the succession proceedings to continue.Overall, the decision highlights how changes in inheritance law can affect ongoing family disputes. The appeals court concluded that differences in signatures and questions surrounding another version of the document were not sufficient to establish that Lloyd's will failed to meet Louisiana's revised legal requirements.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Two eight-year-olds or four four-year-olds': Pakistani cleric's child bride 'joke' sparks outrage
articles.summary: Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood, who commands a large following across social media platforms, has faced criticism over a series of sermons
articles.body: Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood, who commands a large following across social media platforms, has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage.In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.One of the remarks highlighted in the report came from a viral video in which Masood joked that if someone could not find a 16-year-old bride, he could provide “two eight-year-olds” or “four four-year-olds”. The comment drew criticism from people who said it trivialised child marriage and normalised the sexualisation of minors.The Daily Mirror said the backlash was dismissed by supporters as a misunderstanding, with the remark defended as a joke taken out of context.The newspaper also pointed to Masood's repeated opposition to statutory minimum marriage-age laws. According to the report, he has argued that Islamic jurisprudence does not prescribe a universal minimum age of 18 and that parents or guardians should retain discretion over when a girl marries.A recurring theme in his sermons, the newspaper said, is the emphasis on physical development and perceived maturity rather than chronological age when determining whether a girl is ready for marriage. The preacher had made remarks discussing the physical suitability of girls aged nine and ten in the context of marital relations.Pakistan as a country has been grappling with child sexual abuse, forced marriages and gender equality and positioning such leaders as popular figures raises extreme concerns.Education and women's autonomyThe Daily Mirror also highlighted Masood's remarks on women's education, saying that some of his statements appear to place a husband's authority above a young wife's decision to continue her studies.It further cited comments about women marrying late, including references to them becoming “aunties”, and discussions of the benefits husbands derive from marriage.Masood has also been criticised for presenting early marriage as a way to manage men's sexual desiresMasood's sermons have reportedly become difficult to access after copyright complaints and takedown requests. Critics have alleged that this limits public scrutiny of his statements, while his supporters maintain that some remarks are circulated without their original context.Masood has built a substantial following on YouTube, Facebook and other social media platforms through a preaching style that combines religious instruction with informal language and humour. His reach extends beyond traditional religious institutions, particularly among younger and urban audiences.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Civil War steamer sank in Florida in 1864 after striking a Confederate mine; buried beneath river mud, the wreck later yielded more than 3,000 artifacts, including more than 440 linked to Army tents
articles.summary: Discover the fascinating story of the Civil War steamer Maple Leaf, which sank in 1864 after hitting a Confederate mine in Florida. Learn about the recovery operation that unearthed over 3,000 historical artifacts, revealing insights into soldiers' lives during the Civil War.
articles.body: On April 1, 1864, at around 4 am, the Union transport steamer named Maple Leaf was returning from Palatka to Jacksonville along Florida’s St. Johns River. An underwater Confederate mine exploded against the hull of the steamer as soon as it passed Mandarin Point. The blast tore through the vessel, which sank quickly. The vessel took all its military cargo, baggage and personal belongings to the riverbed. The National Park Service reported that four soldiers lost their lives in the disaster.For more than a century, the wreck remained beneath the water's surface. Layers of organic sediment helped preserve the wooden hull and most of its cargo, thus protecting materials that, in a normal scenario, would have deteriorated. When researchers found the wreck in 1984, they uncovered the site, and the operation in 1989 brought more than 3,000 objects to the surface.A Union transport caught in a Confederate minefieldThe Maple Leaf was originally built as a passenger steamship in Kingston, Ontario. Constructed in 1851, the vessel entered service on the Great Lakes the next year. Following a change in ownership, it was sold in 1862 to Boston-based businessmen J.H.B. Lang and Charles Spear. They then chartered the ship to the US Army. The vessel was used by the Union to transport troops and supplies along the eastern seaboard during the Civil War.According to an article published by the Army Historical Foundation, by late March 1864, the Maple Leaf was operating along the St. Johns River. It had carried troops and supplies to Jacksonville before travelling upriver to Palatka. The vessel was carrying the baggage and camp equipment of three Union infantry regiments, which included the 112th New York, the 169th New York and the 13th Indiana, while it was on its return journey.Near the Mandarin Point, Confederate forces had placed underwater explosives to threaten Union shipping. These weapons were commonly known as torpedoes at the time, though they were stationary mines instead of self-propelled devices. On April 1, Maple Leaf struck one of them, and the explosion tore open the hull while the vessel sank in about 20 feet of water.Subsequent archaeological discoveryThe wreck became a hazard to navigation after its sinking. Through contracts in 1873 and 1876, the US Treasury Department attempted to arrange its removal, but the efforts did not result in its sale. In 1882, the US Army Corps of Engineers contracted to move the wreck away from its position in the shipping channel. It is worth noting that this did not mean that the vessel was raised and moved from the riverbed.More than a century after its sinking, Jacksonville dentist and diver Keith Holland became interested in locating the vessel. By studying the old river chart and comparing it with the modern maps, he and his co-workers narrowed down the likely location. In 1984, Holland and the St. Johns Archaeological Expeditions team located the wreck beneath several feet of organic silt. Interestingly, this discovery was followed by negotiations over ownership and salvage rights because both Florida and the federal government had claims to the site.The discovery did not immediately prompt a full-scale recovery. The team instead had to address legal and property questions and develop procedures for excavating and conserving objects that had remained underwater for more than a century. Eventually, the archaeological work led to a major recovery operation in 1989. It went on for 10 days, and the team brought more than 3,000 objects to the surface.The 3,000 objects reveal insight into soldiers’ livesThe recovered collection mostly included military equipment, uniform-related items, personal belongings, bottles, smoking pipes and objects related to soldiers’ daily routines. According to the Mandarin Museum, organic matter in the sediment consumed much of the oxygen available, thus slowing the deterioration of wooden and leather objects. However, once they were exposed to air, the materials reportedly became very vulnerable to rapid decay. The team used various methods, including chemical treatments, to stabilise the findings.Among the notable finds were more than 440 artifacts linked with Army tents, according to Ephraim D. Dickson III, a historian with the US Army Center of Military History. Wooden tent poles, rope fittings and oak tent pegs were all recovered from the wreck. As such equipment rarely survives from the Civil War period, the collection is valuable for understanding how soldiers established and maintained their camps. The wreck now remains beneath the St. Johns River, buried in sediment and closed to recreational diving.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A retired Canadian man learned the $50 million Lotto Max ticket was sold in his county but waited to check his own to ‘keep the dream alive’; all seven numbers matched, and his teacher wife can now retire
articles.summary: Retired New Brunswick resident Shaun Ryan held the winning ticket to a $50m Lotto Max jackpot for days before checking it, choosing to delay the reveal
articles.body: Retired New Brunswick resident Shaun Ryan held the winning ticket to a $50m Lotto Max jackpot for days before checking it, choosing to delay the reveal simply to enjoy the anticipation. The Atlantic Lottery announced on 10 November that Ryan, a resident of Dalhousie, a small town on Chaleur Bay in Restigouche County, successfully matched all seven numbers in the 6 November draw to take home the massive $50m prize. The decision to delay checking the ticket came after local chatter alerted Ryan that the sole winning ticket for the draw had been purchased somewhere within his home county. “My wife asked if we had a ticket and then my son texted me and asked if we bought one,” Ryan said in statements released by the Atlantic Lottery. “My wife asked if I was going to go check it and I said, 'No, not yet. I want to keep the dream alive.'” When Ryan eventually checked the numbers at his home, he realised every single digit on his slip aligned with the drawn combination. “Boom, boom, boom,” Ryan recalled of the moment he verified the results. “My heart was racing.”A milestone for the householdThe multi-million-pound payout carries immediate life-changing news for the household. While Ryan is already retired, his wife, Colette, works as a teacher. The jackpot win means she can now step away from the classroom for good. The couple already possess differing views on how to spend their new-found freedom. Colette intends to spend her retirement traveling the globe. Ryan, on the other hand, prefers a quieter lifestyle and plans to stay at home to look after the family dogs. Securing the future of their large family remains the top shared priority. Ryan explained that a major portion of the funds will go directly toward supporting their seven children and their grandchildren.Supporting the local regionBeyond family allocations, Ryan expressed a clear desire to distribute a portion of the windfall toward community initiatives within northern New Brunswick. “There's a responsibility I feel toward the community and organizations that I want to be of service to and help them out in certain ways,” Ryan noted. “Fifty million dollars is a heavy load, and there's a lot to think of because there's a lot that could be done for the community.” While the Atlantic Lottery statement did not outline specific charities or projects earmarked for funding, Ryan acknowledged the sheer scale of the win remains difficult to grasp completely. “It's just unreal,” Ryan said. “It's a little overwhelming, but I'm happy to have the chance to feel it.”Retailer commission and tax rulesThe jackpot win also represents a significant financial event for the local business that processed the entry. According to rules set by the Atlantic Lottery, the retail vendor receives a seller's prize equivalent to one per cent of the total jackpot. Consequently, the Circle K convenience store in Dalhousie where Ryan bought his ticket will receive a $500,000 payout. Under Canadian tax regulations enforced by the Canada Revenue Agency, lottery jackpots are not treated as taxable income. Ryan will collect the entire $50m figure tax-free, though any future interest, investment returns, or capital gains generated from the capital will be subject to standard taxation.Recent Canadian lottery trendsRyan's multi-million-pound ticket arrived just 17 days after another massive payout in Western Canada. In the 20 October Lotto Max draw, four friends located in Calgary, Alberta, shared a record-breaking $90m jackpot, taking home $22.5m each. While Ryan delayed checking his ticket for a short period to savor the moment, other regional players have pushed deadlines far closer to the edge. Atlantic Lottery records show that crab fisherman Merel Chiasson from Bas-Caraquet, New Brunswick, left a winning Lotto 6/49 ticket on his bedroom dresser for 347 days following an April 2023 draw. Chiasson validated the slip just 19 days before its official expiration date to claim a $64m Gold Ball jackpot, which stood as the largest lottery payout in Atlantic Canadian history prior to recent draws.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jess Phillips calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse
articles.summary: New technology would block the live-streaming of child sexual abuse on phones, tablets and laptops.
articles.body:
Former safeguarding minister Jess Phillips has joined calls from campaigners for the government to back new technology that blocks the live-streaming of child sexual abuse.

The UK National Crime Agency has flagged the UK as the third biggest market in the world for live-streamed abuse, where children are sexually abused live on camera to order.

Device-level blockers can prevent this material being filmed and viewed on smartphones, laptops and tablets in the first place, Phillips said, at the launch of a policy report in Parliament.

Anti-abuse campaigners claim keeping the technology at device level maintains privacy and encryption. Civil liberties campaigners Big Brother Watch dispute this.

The government has already legislated to demand tech firms like Apple and Google, which develop the operating systems of most smartphones used in the UK, block under-18s from taking or sharing nude images on smartphones and other devices.

However, three-quarters of child sexual abuse material (CSA) was not self-generated but likely captured on adult devices, according to 2025 research from the Internet Watch Foundation (IWF), which works to eliminate child sexual abuse imagery online.

Some 1.8 million men in the UK admitted to some form of online sexual offending against children, according to research from child safety institute Childlight.

Phillips, who complained of repeated delays to work to tackle CSA when she resigned as safeguarding minister in May, is demanding action to tackle the source of the crime and reduce the number of British offenders.

"This should be a source of national shame, and we must stop it," the Labour MP said.

"The technology, the evidence and the public support are all there - I want to work with ministers to extend on-device blocking to child sexual abuse material on every device sold in Britain, making children here and over the world safer."

The software uses AI to classify known child abuse images in the phone's operating system, and blocks the material at the moment it is viewed or created, whatever app is in use.

Nothing is logged, stored or sent anywhere, and the tech would work alongside encryption.

The AI classifier has been trained against a database of known child abuse images so it can differentiate between harmless material such as children at the beach, and sexual abuse.

Phillips said online child sexual abuse is "an issue that we did not keep control of" as legislators and now must be prioritised, at the event in Parliament.

She was joined by survivors of online child sexual abuse, who said they should not have to beg for the removal of images of themselves being abused from the internet.

Phil Eccles, from the National Crime Agency (NCA), said the scale of the problem was "at crisis point".

"This would cut off at source somebody on the UK their ability to direct a live stream for a child to be abused," he said.

"To me, safeguarding children will always supersede the ability to prosecute. If we can stop that abuse we must.

"But it's so important that tech companies come onboard - we cannot arrest our way out of this problem."

New law to force tech firms to stop children taking or sharing nude images

What the Online Safety Act is - and how to keep children safe online

UK police bosses say unsafe social media platforms should be blocked for under-16s

The parliamentary briefing also heard from the former minister, Conservative Lord Nash, who led the campaign for an under-16s social media ban.

He said: "By the time the police are involved, a child has already been abused and the images and videos have gone round the globe.

"The material has to be blocked on the phone itself, before the harm is done.

"The government deserves real credit for committing to exactly that on children's phones.

"I urge it now to extend that commitment to every device sold in Britain, targeted at CSA material, and to lead the world in doing so."

In a sign of CSA becoming more prevalent, communications watchdog Ofcom has found almost as many offenders looking for CSA on everyday apps on the open web as on the dark web.

John Tanagho, from the anti-trafficking organisation the International Justice Mission, highlighted how children in poorer countries were being targeted for sexual exploitation, with research showing one in every 100 Filipino children were victims.

Legislation should explicitly limit the scans to CSA material, he said, with no data shared with the government or any private companies, maintaining privacy.

A government spokesperson said: "We are putting in place the strongest online safety laws in the world.

"This includes preparing world-first legislation to call on the biggest technology companies to make it impossible for children to take, share or view nude images.

"We will also give the police the powers they need to keep pace with criminal use of emerging technologies in order to keep our children safe."

articles.title: Transit officials looking into 'unsafe' incident where 2 horses boarded public bus
articles.summary: Video shows two people leading the saddled horses onto the bus.
articles.body:
Transit officials in Detroit said they are looking into a recent incident in which two horses were captured on video briefly boarding a public bus.

The Detroit Department of Transportation (DDOT) said in a statement Tuesday that it is "aware of a recent incident where two horses were allowed to walk through a bus as it was pulled over at a bus stop."

Video of the incident shows two people leading two saddled horses onto the bus while it was pulled over at the stop, then exiting from the rear doors several seconds later.

"We are taking appropriate steps to address this incident as it is not consistent with DDOT policy and potentially creates an unsafe and uncomfortable ride for our passengers," DDOT said.

The incident occurred Saturday along 7 Mile East near Strasburg Street.

Ellessia Drew was driving down 7 Mile when she stopped to film the incident.

"I was thinking, like, 'Oh my God, like what about the people on the bus? What if the horse used the bathroom on the bus? Like, what's going on?'" Drew told ABC Detroit affiliate WXYZ .

The animals' owner, Jordan Williams, with the group Urban City Cowboys, told WXYZ that he has brought horses on Detroit buses before.

"It's not my first rodeo," he told the station.

He said he had been at an event giving children horseback rides on Saturday. When he saw the bus pull up, he said he asked the driver if he could take his "service animal" on board for a video, with the goal of highlighting Black cowboys in Detroit.

"The point is just to bring light to the city that there are cowboys that look like us," Williams told WXZY.

According to Williams, there were two or three passengers on the bus at the time and nobody got hurt.

"I hope DDOT looks at it as a joke like everyone else, and hopefully maybe come out to a rodeo," Williams told WXYZ.

DDOT noted that only service animals are allowed on buses and "must be under control by the person with disabilities at all times, must not occupy a seat, and must either sit on the floor, or on the person's lap."

articles.title: Russian ambassador to US Alexander Darchiev dies 'suddenly' at 66

articles.body: Russia's ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, died a sudden death on Wednesday, at the age of 66, the Russian foreign ministry said."The Russian Foreign Ministry announces with profound sorrow that Alexander Darchiev, Ambassador of Russia to the USA, passed away suddenly on November 11, aged 66. articles.title: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library distributed over 537,000 free books in Michigan's Muskegon County over 11 years; now set to shut down as $180,000 annual funding shortfall forces closure
articles.summary: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, a popular children's literacy programme that has provided free books to thousands of families, is set to end in
articles.body: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, a popular children's literacy programme that has provided free books to thousands of families, is set to end in Muskegon County, Michigan, after more than a decade. United Way of the Lakeshore has announced that it will discontinue the initiative, with the final book mailing scheduled for December 2026. The decision comes after the nonprofit struggled to secure sustainable funding to meet the programme's annual operating costs of approximately $180,000.In a statement cited by mLive, United Way of the Lakeshore said reductions in state and local funding had created a financial shortfall that the organisation could no longer cover. Despite exploring several funding alternatives, it was unable to identify a sustainable way to continue the programme.Lisa Tyler, president and CEO of United Way of the Lakeshore, acknowledged the disappointment the decision would bring to families while highlighting the initiative's achievements over the years."We share the sadness and disappointment that so many families are feeling, but we are also incredibly proud of the legacy we've built together," Tyler said.She added that more than half a million books had reached homes across Muskegon County, giving children and their families opportunities to read, learn and grow together.Programme distributed over 537,000 free books since 2015The Imagination Library initiative was launched in Muskegon County in 2015, initially covering just two communities. Over the years, it expanded into a county-wide programme, distributing more than 537,000 books to local children at no cost to their families.The initiative is part of Dolly Parton's wider Imagination Library, which aims to encourage childhood literacy by providing age-appropriate books to young children.Before announcing the closure, United Way of the Lakeshore explored potential funding partnerships with school districts, library systems, literacy-focused nonprofits and community donors. However, these efforts did not produce the long-term financial support required to maintain the programme.Dolly Parton's Imagination Library to continue in Oceana CountyWhile the programme will end in Muskegon County, it will continue operating in neighbouring Oceana County. According to United Way of the Lakeshore, the smaller population and different financial requirements there make it possible to sustain the initiative with the available resources.There is also a possibility that the programme could return to Muskegon County through a new local partnership. An eligible nonprofit, faith-based organisation, school system or local government could establish an affiliate partnership with Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, provided it secures adequate funding and develops a sustainable operational plan.United Way to continue other children's literacy programmesDespite ending its involvement with the Imagination Library in Muskegon County, United Way of the Lakeshore has said it will continue supporting childhood literacy through its other initiatives.These include its Early Childhood Literacy Programme, which connects trained volunteer mentors with students who need additional reading assistance.Reaffirming the organisation's commitment to children's education, Tyler said the closure of the Imagination Library would not mean an end to its literacy efforts."While we are closing this chapter of the Imagination Library, we are not stepping away from the work of helping children become strong readers," she said.She added that the organisation would continue working with schools, supporting literacy-focused organisations and bringing communities together to help children succeed.The final book mailing in December 2026 will mark the end of a programme that has distributed more than half a million free books to children in Muskegon County since its launch in 2015.You use AI every day. articles.title: North Korea revises constitution, calls South Korea separate state & drops reunification goal
articles.summary: North Korea has released the full text of its revised constitution, formally defining South Korea as a separate neighbouring country and removing
articles.body: North Korea has released the full text of its revised constitution, formally defining South Korea as a separate neighbouring country and removing references to reunification, in a further step towards institutionalising leader Kim Jong-un's policy of treating the two Koreas as hostile states.The revised document, published on Wednesday on the North Korean propaganda website Naenara, also expands Kim's authority over the country's nuclear forces, including allowing him to delegate the power to use nuclear weapons to the state nuclear command organisation.According to the Korea JoongAng Daily, the constitution was amended at the first session of the 15th Supreme People's Assembly on March 23. Its publication ends a period of more than two and a half years during which Pyongyang had made the constitutional text inaccessible online.The most significant change is in Article 2, which defines North Korea's territory as the land bordering China and Russia to the north and the Republic of Korea to the south, along with the territorial waters and airspace associated with it. The provision explicitly names South Korea as a separate country sharing a border with the North, although it does not specify the precise land or maritime boundaries.The revised constitution removes provisions on national reunification that appeared in the previous version.Kim's authority over nuclear forces expandedThe revised text also strengthens the constitutional powers of the chairman of the State Affairs Commission, a post held by Kim. It places the country's nuclear forces under the chairman's command and allows the leader to delegate authority to use nuclear weapons to the state nuclear command organisation.The changes formalise Kim's control over the country's nuclear arsenal at a time when Pyongyang has increasingly emphasised its nuclear capabilities and the possibility of retaliation against attacks on its leadership.The newly published constitution largely corresponds with a revised version obtained and released by South Korea's Ministry of Unification in May, the Korea JoongAng Daily reported.However, the public text omits portions of two articles. One concerns the Cabinet's authority to adopt resolutions at plenary meetings, while the other deals with the election of lay judges to special courts. It is unclear whether these passages were removed during the constitutional revision or excluded when the version was prepared for publication.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Amanda Seyfried says her nine-year-old daughter watched 'Mean Girls' for the first time last year and loved it; the actress has revealed how she decides which of her own movies her children are ready to see
articles.summary: Amanda Seyfried is a name almost every ‘Mean Girl’ lover knows.
articles.body: Amanda Seyfried is a name almost every ‘Mean Girl’ lover knows. The Hollywood actor who is a mother now to a nine-year-old daughter has her own memories of watching the movie. When kids begin discovering what their parents do beyond their roles at home, even familiar things can suddenly become fascinating.The 2004 teen comedy, in which Seyfried played Karen Smith, has remained a pop culture favourite for over two decades now. And introducing the film to Nina was really interesting. According to the actor, her daughter enjoyed watching her on screen, although her reaction to the film itself was refreshingly honest.In an interview with E! News at the world premiere of her upcoming film Steps in New York, Seyfried spoke about how her kids are gradually becoming familiar with her work. The 40-year-old actor shares two children, daughter Nina, 9, and son Thomas Jr., 6, with actor Thomas Sadoski."They've seen the few animated movies I've done," she told the publication, adding that her daughter watched Mean Girls for the first time last year. "They love it."However, an earlier conversation with Vogue offered a more detailed glimpse into Nina's response. Seyfried revealed that her daughter, who was eight at the time, did not find the film particularly funny. But she loved her mother's performance.When children see their parents in a different lightFor most children, parents are simply the people who prepare their meals, help with homework, attend school meetings and take care of everyday responsibilities. Discovering that their mother or father has another identity outside the home can be an exciting experience."It's normal for them," she told the publication, referring to growing up with a mother whose work involves films, premieres and public appearances."I'm learning more every day. I think as they get older, they're like, 'Huh, what a very unique place to get to be.' I'm like, 'Yeah, it is unique!'" she said.Kids reactions for their famous parentsChildren may initially find it difficult to understand what their parents do, but experiences such as watching a film, visiting a workplace or seeing a parent interact with colleagues can gradually help them appreciate another side of their personality.For Seyfried, sharing her work with her children also appears to be about finding projects they can enjoy together rather than simply introducing them to her filmography.Why watching a parent's work can become a special experienceInterestingly, Mean Girls was not the first film through which Nina became familiar with her mother's acting career. Ninal already loves Seyfried's 2008 musical romantic comedy Mamma Mia!.In an earlier interview with People in 2024, the actor revealed that Nina had watched the film with her grandmother and had become particularly fond of it. She also enjoyed its sequel, Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again, and the music featuring songs by ABBA.Seyfried recalled that her daughter's friends had also started recognising her as Sophie, the character she plays in the musical films. For the actor, seeing her daughter develop an appreciation for something she had worked on was a rather special experience.A new generation discovering old favouritesSeyfried is now preparing to introduce her children to another of her projects, Steps, an animated reimagining of the Cinderella story. The film features Ali Wong and Stephanie Hsu as misunderstood stepsisters who join forces to save their kingdom from a childhood bully, played by Nikki Glaser. It is scheduled to premiere on Netflix on November 20, 2026.Explaining what she liked about the film, Seyfried said it explores the complexities of relationships, sisterhood and friendship, particularly the importance of communication and understanding."It's beautiful," she said, adding that it was the kind of film she wanted her children to watch.For Seyfried, seeing her children discover her work seems to be an evolving experience. Nina may not yet share the same enthusiasm for every film that made her mother famous, but her honest reactions are perhaps what make these moments memorable.And that is a useful reminder for parents: children do not have to love everything their parents love. Sometimes, allowing them to form their own opinions, ask questions and express their preferences is what makes sharing experiences meaningful.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: HC pulls up HYDRAA chief, asks DGP to ensure his appearance on Nov 17
articles.summary: Telangana HC directs DGP to ensure HYDRAA chief AV Ranganath appears Nov 17 in Shamshabad land demolition contempt case; tahsildar too.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Taking a serious view of HYDRAA commissioner AV Ranganath’s alleged failure to comply with court directions, the Telangana high court on Wednesday directed the state’s director general of police to ensure that the agency chief personally appears before it on Nov 17. It also directed Cyberabad police to ensure that Shamshabad tahsildar Amar Lingam appears before the court along with Ranganath on the same day.Justice CV Bhaskar Reddy passed the directions while hearing a contempt case filed by Mohammed Tajamaluddin over the alleged demolition of a structure on 43,560 square yards (about 9 acres) of land in Shamshabad in violation of court directions. The judge also dismissed separate interlocutory applications filed by the HYDRAA commissioner and the tahsildar, seeking exemption from personal appearance.The case pertains to land owned by Tajamaluddin, which was placed on the prohibited properties list under Section 22-A of the Registration Act. In Oct 2024, Justice Bhaskar Reddy permitted the petitioner to file an application along with documents supporting his right and title, seeking removal of the land from the prohibited list.The court directed the authorities to examine the application, take necessary steps and pass a reasoned order in accordance with law, provided the petitioner fulfilled the prescribed conditions.However, Tajamaluddin alleged that HYDRAA took forcible possession of his property without issuing any notice and in violation of the principles of natural justice. It allegedly “dismantled the existing structure and erected fencing, along with a nameplate declaring that the property belongs to the govt”.Contending that the petitioner was the absolute owner of the land and was in possession since the 1980s, the petitioner’s counsel submitted that despite the court’s directions, the tahsildar and HYDRAA commissioner had forcibly taken possession of the property and urged the court to punish the officials for contempt of court.During its previous hearing on Oct 13, the court had issued notices directing both officials to appear before it on Nov 11. articles.title: HC takes up PIL claiming ₹5k crore realty fraud
articles.summary: Telangana HC admits PIL alleging ₹5,000 crore Spectra Group realty fraud in Hyderabad; claims 10,000+ homebuyers duped, seeks court-monitored SIT probe.
articles.body: Hyderabad: High court has admitted a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) alleging a massive real estate fraud of over ₹5,000 crore by companies operating under the name of Hyderabad-based Spectra Group, allegedly duping more than 10,000 homebuyers and investors across Telangana.A bench comprising Acting Chief Justice P Sam Koshy and Justice Suddala Chalapathi Rao directed the group to file counters in response to the PIL filed by a city-based NGO The Right Society, represented by its president A Venkateswara Reddy, and adjourned the matter for further hearing.Senior Counsel B Rachana Reddy, appearing for the petitioner, contended that Spectra India Eco Projects Pvt Ltd, Spectra India Housing Pvt Ltd, Spectra India Mega Projects Pvt Ltd and their associated companies collected money from the public since 2015 by promising residential plots, approved layouts and housing projects.The petitioner alleged that the companies mobilised over ₹5,000 crore from more than 10,000 customers through a network of nearly 10,000 marketing agents.“Around 15 projects spread over more than 2,000 acres were marketed within 70-80 km of Hyderabad. These included Spectra Galaxy Divine at Kolanpak, Spectra Yashovan and Galaxy Gold at Yadagirigutta, Spectra Diamond at Yadadri, Highway City at Narketpally, Viceroy Residency, Fortune, Fortune Residency, Peripheral City, Spectra City and Viceroy phases at Shadnagar, Gateway City at Balanagar and Spectra Tech Towers at Injapur-Uppal,” the petitioner said in the petition.The petitioner alleged that several projects were abandoned without developing basic infrastructure or executing sale deeds despite collecting money from buyers.Rachana Reddy further argued that only six projects obtained RERA registration and that mandatory escrow accounts were not maintained, resulting in diversion of funds.The petition also presented details of dishonoured post-dated cheques issued by the group and misleading claims about HMDA and DTCP approvals to allegedly convince and dupe investors.Alleging that RERA, police, Enforcement Directorate, Economic Offences Wing, SFIO, SEBI and other enforcement agencies failed to initiate a coordinated investigation despite receiving representations, the petitioner sought a direction for a court-monitored Special Investigation Team (SIT), registration of criminal cases under the Telangana Protection of Depositors of Financial Establishments Act and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, forensic audits of the companies and completion of abandoned projects.It also sought freezing and attachment of the companies’ and directors’ assets to protect investors’ money.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: MCD steps up ghat inspections ahead of Chhath Puja
articles.summary: MCD intensifies Chhath Puja ghat inspections in Delhi, preparing 1,400+ sites; orders cleanup of Yamuna waste, better sanitation, lights and dustbins.
articles.body: New Delhi: With Chhath Puja preparations gathering pace, Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has stepped up inspections at ghats across the capital to ensure proper sanitation, cleanliness and facilities for devotees. More than 1,400 ghats have been prepared across the city this year.At Haathi Ghat near ITO, East Zone deputy commissioner Azharuddin Zaheeruddin Qazi reviewed preparations and flagged waste accumulated along parts of the riverbank and floating garbage in Yamuna. Officials were directed to clear the riverbank immediately and coordinate with the Irrigation and Flood Control Department to remove floating waste using motorised boats.MCD said sanitation arrangements at the ghat were satisfactory, with workers deployed for regular cleaning. Officials were also asked to ensure the prompt removal of construction and demolition waste from all ghats.In southwest Delhi, MP Kamaljeet Sehrawat inspected preparations at ghats in Sagarpur and Mahavir Enclave. In west Delhi, ward committee chairman Harish Oberoi and deputy commissioner Col Vinod Atri reviewed arrangements at New Krishna Park ghat in Vikaspuri.Officials said all zones have been directed to complete preparations on time, including installation of lights and placement of dustbins.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Namo Bharat Trains Cross 5 Crore Passenger Journeys
articles.summary: Namo Bharat trains on the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS cross 5 crore passenger journeys since Oct 2023, with monthly ridership above 32 lakh.
articles.body: New Delhi: Namo Bharat trains have recorded a milestone, with over five crore passenger journeys since operations began on the corridor on Oct 21, 2023. It registered over 32 lakh passenger journeys every month during Aug, Sept and Oct this year, indicating sustained passenger demand.With the inauguration of the 17-km priority section in Oct 2023 between Sahibabad and Duhai Depot, it took 574 days to record the first one crore passenger journeys on May 16 last year. From there, commuter uptake accelerated sharply. The corridor achieved its two-crore ridership mark on Dec 11, 2025, in 211 days. This year, it crossed the three crore mark on May 2, in 143 days, and reached four crore on Aug 10, in just 101 days. “Carrying this aggressive momentum forward, the corridor logged its five-crore milestone on Nov 10, adding the latest one crore journeys in a record 93-day interval,” said an official of National Capital Region Transport Corporation, which is implementing the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS corridor.The corridor has also witnessed sustained passenger movement over the last three months. In Aug 2026, it recorded 35.3 lakh passenger journeys, with an average daily ridership of 1,13,708. Its highest-ever single-day ridership was also recorded on Aug 28 at 1,68,666 passenger journeys. Sept registered 32.4 lakh journeys, with an average daily ridership of 1,08,043, while Oct recorded 33.5 lakh passenger journeys, with an average daily ridership of 1,08,049.“The consistent monthly ridership reflects the growing use of Namo Bharat for everyday travel,” said the official. He added that Namo Bharat has significantly improved travel between Delhi, Ghaziabad and Meerut. Faster connectivity, air-conditioned coaches, reliable train operations and convenient interchange facilities have made regional journeys more feasible for commuters travelling for work, education, business and other purposes.Seamless integration with other modes of public transport, including Delhi Metro, Indian Railways, interstate bus terminals and city bus services, and integration of Meerut Metro services with Namo Bharat over the same infrastructure are central to this enhanced commuter experience, added the official.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
